ei.title: Making the Audience Care for Characters
ei.subject: 올림포스전국연합고1_2026

fullPassage: What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author to establish a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be recognizable as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be emotionally invested in a character as either ally or enemy.

questions.passage: What does it mean for a character to be a (A)[fool / hero] as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author to establish a (B)[hostile / positive] relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be (C)[recognizable / invisible] as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be emotionally invested in a character as either ally or enemy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) hero=영웅, (B) positive=긍정적인, (C) recognizable=식별 가능한
det.analysis:
✅ ① hero — positive — recognizable: 원문 일치. 악당과 대비되는 영웅(hero), 작가가 수립하는 긍정적(positive) 관계, 친구/적으로 식별 가능한(recognizable) 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② fool — positive — recognizable: (A) fool(바보)은 villain과 대비되는 hero와 다름
❌ ③ hero — hostile — recognizable: (B) hostile(적대적인)은 '긍정적 관계'라는 positive와 반대
❌ ④ hero — positive — invisible: (C) invisible(보이지 않는)은 '식별 가능한'이라는 recognizable과 반대
det.tip: hero as opposed to a villain / positive relationship / recognizable as friend or enemy

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) essential=필수적인, (B) benefit=이익을 주다, (C) worthy=가치 있는
det.analysis:
❌ ① optional — benefit — worthy: (A) optional(선택적인)은 '필수적'이라는 essential과 반대
❌ ② essential — harm — worthy: (B) harm(해를 끼치다)은 주인공의 행동이 우리에게 '이익을 준다'는 benefit과 반대
❌ ③ essential — benefit — useless: (C) useless(쓸모없는)는 '가치 있는 동반자'라는 worthy와 반대
✅ ④ essential — benefit — worthy: 원문 일치. 긍정적 관계 수립이 필수적(essential)이고, 주인공의 행동이 우리에게 이익을 주며(benefit), 가치 있는(worthy) 동반자라는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: it's essential / actions benefit us / a worthy companion

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) adjusted=조정된, (B) incidental=부수적인, (C) invested=몰입한
det.analysis:
❌ ① ignored — incidental — invested: (A) ignored(무시된)는 인물이 '조정되어야' 한다는 adjusted와 다름
✅ ② adjusted — incidental — invested: 원문 일치. 인물이 식별 가능하도록 조정되고(adjusted), 단역의 부수적(incidental) 죽음, 관객이 인물에 몰입해야(invested) 한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ③ adjusted — central — invested: (B) central(중심적인)은 '부수적인' 단역의 죽음이라는 incidental과 반대
❌ ④ adjusted — incidental — detached: (C) detached(초연한)는 감정적으로 '몰입한'이라는 invested와 반대
det.tip: character must be adjusted / incidental deaths / emotionally invested

In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author to ②<u>establish</u> a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be ③<u>adjusted</u> so as to be recognizable as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions ④<u>harm</u> us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be emotionally invested in a character as either ally or enemy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ harm(해를 끼치다) → benefit(이익을 주다): 주인공의 행동은 우리에게 이익을 준다는 맥락
det.analysis:
✅ ① hero: '영웅(hero)인가 악당인가'라는 도입 — 문맥 적절
✅ ② establish: '긍정적 관계를 수립하다(establish)' — 문맥 적절
✅ ③ adjusted: '인물이 식별 가능하도록 조정되다(adjusted)' — 문맥 적절
❌ ④ harm → benefit: 'someone whose actions benefit us'에서 주인공의 행동은 우리에게 이익을 준다(benefit). harm(해를 끼치다)으로 바꾸면 '가치 있는 동반자'라는 맥락과 모순 ←정답
det.tip: actions benefit us = 행동이 우리에게 이익을 준다 / harm은 반대

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

✅ ③ worthy: '가치 있는(worthy) 동반자' — 문맥 적절

det.korean: ③ weak(약한) → strong(강한): 강한 감정을 느끼기 위해 인물에 몰입해야 함

❌ ③ (A) (그림을) 그리다 — (B) 비기다: (B)의 draw out은 '이끌어내다'이지 비기다가 아님
❌ ④ (A) 뽑다 — (B) 다가가다: 두 의미 모두 부적절
det.tip: draw: ① 그리다 ② draw out = 이끌어내다 ③ 비기다 ④ 끌어당기다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the main character in a story, film, or play"

det.korean: protagonist=주인공 (이야기·영화·연극의 주요 인물)
det.analysis:
❌ ① villain: villain(악당)은 주인공과 대비되는 악역
✅ ② protagonist: protagonist(주인공)는 이야기·영화·연극의 주요 인물로 영영 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ audience: audience(관객)는 작품을 보는 사람
❌ ④ author: author(작가)는 작품을 만드는 사람
det.tip: protagonist = 주인공. the main character가 핵심

questions.passage: Violent action films are often __________ (fill) with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be emotionally invested in a character as either ally or enemy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: be동사(are) + 과거분사(p.p.) 수동태 — be filled with(~로 가득 차다)
det.analysis: 주어 films가 '채워지는' 대상이므로 수동태가 필요하다. 'are often ______ with'이므로 fill의 과거분사 filled가 와야 한다. be filled with = ~로 가득 차 있다.
det.tip: be filled with = ~로 가득 차다 (수동태, p.p. filled)

questions.passage: We must feel that the protagonist is someone whose __________ (act) benefit us. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 소유격 관계대명사 whose 뒤 명사 + 복수 동사(benefit) → 복수 명사 actions
det.analysis: 소유격 관계대명사 whose 뒤에는 명사가 와야 하고, 뒤의 동사가 benefit(복수형)이므로 복수 명사 actions가 되어야 한다. whose actions benefit us = 그의 행동이 우리에게 이익을 주는.
det.tip: act(동사) → actions(복수 명사). whose + 명사 + 동사

questions.passage: What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author to establish a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be recognizable as __________. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be emotionally invested in a character as either ally or enemy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: either friend or enemy=친구 또는 적 — 인물이 둘 중 하나로 식별되어야 함
det.analysis:
❌ ① beyond all recognition(전혀 알아볼 수 없게): 식별 가능해야 한다는 맥락과 반대
❌ ② a minor background figure(사소한 배경 인물): 식별 대상의 선/악 구분과 무관
❌ ③ part of the anonymous crowd(익명의 군중의 일부): 식별 가능성과 반대
✅ ④ either friend or enemy: 원문 일치. 'recognizable as ______'에서 인물은 친구 또는 적(either friend or enemy)으로 식별 가능해야 함 ←정답
det.tip: recognizable as either friend or enemy = 친구 또는 적으로 식별 가능한

questions.passage: What does it mean for a character to be a hero as opposed to a villain? In artistic and entertainment descriptions, it's essential for the author to establish a positive relationship between a protagonist and the audience. In order for tragedy or misfortune to draw out an emotional response in viewers, the character must be adjusted so as to be recognizable as either friend or enemy. Whether the portrayal is fictional or documentary, we must feel that the protagonist is someone whose actions benefit us; the protagonist is, or would be, a worthy companion or valued ally. Violent action films are often filled with dozens of incidental deaths of minor characters that draw out little response in the audience. In order to feel strong emotions, the audience must be __________ as either ally or enemy.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: emotionally invested in a character=인물에 감정적으로 몰입한 — 강한 감정을 느끼기 위한 조건
det.analysis:
❌ ① completely unaware of the events(사건을 전혀 모르는): 강한 감정을 느끼는 조건과 반대
❌ ② bored by the entire storyline(줄거리에 지루해하는): 몰입과 반대
✅ ③ emotionally invested in a character: 원문 일치. 'the audience must be ______'에서 강한 감정을 느끼려면 관객이 인물에 감정적으로 몰입해야(emotionally invested) 함 ←정답
❌ ④ distracted from the main plot(주요 줄거리에서 산만해진): 몰입과 반대
det.tip: emotionally invested in a character = 인물에 감정적으로 몰입한
